title: The neuroscience of delirium: a perfect storm for acute brain dysfunction
title_zh: 谵妄的神经科学：急性大脑功能障碍的完美风暴
abstract: Delirium is a frequent and distressing neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by acute disturbances of attention, awareness and cognition. Delirium emerges in response to diverse medical insults, particularly in hospitalized patients. Despite its high prevalence and association with accelerated cognitive decline, dementia and mortality, the neurobiology of delirium remains incompletely understood, and there are no treatments for delirium. Evidence from electrophysiology, neuroimaging, biomarkers and emerging animal models has begun to clarify the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying delirium. Delirium can be conceptualized as the interaction of acute systemic or cerebral stressors with pre-existing vulnerabilities, creating a ‘perfect storm’ for brain dysfunction. Generalized electroencephalographic slowing and network disintegration are convergent signatures across diverse types of delirium. Disruptions in neuromodulatory systems, energy metabolism and neuroimmune signalling may underlie impairment of large-scale brain function. The mechanisms that drive acute delirium may also contribute to subsequent brain injury and long-term decline, compounding its broad personal and societal impact. Delirium is a highly prevalent, but much neglected, acute neuropsychiatric syndrome strongly associated with dementia. In this Review, Cunningham and Kimchi detail the neurophysiological and neuroanatomical basis of delirium and the metabolic and neuroinflammatory mechanisms that may drive it.
abstract_zh: 谵妄是一种常见且令人痛苦的神经精神综合征，其特征是注意力、意识和认知的急性紊乱。谵妄通常在各种医疗损伤反应中出现，尤其是在住院患者中。尽管其患病率高，且与认知功能加速下降、痴呆和死亡率相关，但谵妄的神经生物学机制仍未完全阐明，目前尚无治疗谵妄的方法。电生理学、神经影像学、生物标志物以及新兴动物模型的证据已开始阐明谵妄背后的病理生理机制。谵妄可被概念化为急性系统性或脑部压力源与既往易感性之间的相互作用，从而为大脑功能障碍创造“完美风暴”。广泛脑电图慢波和网络解体是多种谵妄类型中的共同标志。神经调节系统、能量代谢和神经免疫信号传导的紊乱可能导致大尺度大脑功能受损。驱动急性谵妄的机制也可能导致随后的脑损伤和长期认知下降，加剧其对个人和社会的广泛影响。谵妄是一种高度普遍但被严重忽视的急性神经精神综合征，与痴呆关系密切。在本综述中，Cunningham 和 Kimchi 阐述了谵妄的神经生理和神经解剖学基础，以及可能驱动其发生的代谢和神经炎症机制。
